Author: GitHixy
Name: HitSpark
Description:
HitSpark replaces Final Fantasy XIV's combat text with its own renderer: better fonts, tuned motion and real impact on critical hits.

WHAT YOU GET

- Every kind of combat text redrawn: damage dealt and taken, healing, misses and evades, status effects, experience, crafting and loot.
- Eight built-in presets, each a complete look: Classic+, Heroic, Tally, Onslaught, Elemental, Grim, Minimal and Retro.
- Real motion: arcs, fountains, rising and falling paths, scrolling columns, and punch, shake, flash, sparks and trails on crits.
- Multi-hits and damage over time that roll up into one number, with DoT ticks in their own colour.
- Other players' numbers shown smaller, or hidden, for your party and for everyone else.
- A style editor for every category with a live preview, and presets you can share as a short code.

GETTING STARTED

Type /hitspark (or /hs) to open the settings and pick a preset. /hitspark test plays sample numbers on you and your target, even out of combat.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you.

PLAYS BY THE RULES

HitSpark is purely cosmetic: it only redraws text the game already shows you and follows the game's own flying text and pop-up text options. If a game update breaks it, the game's own numbers come back on their own. Settings and presets are stored locally and nothing is ever sent anywhere.
Punchline: Replace the game's combat numbers with animated, styleable fly text.

Author: GitHixy
Name: FateLimit
Description:
FateLimit draws the border of FATE areas right in the world, so you always know where the fight ends and never lose your level sync by wandering out.

WHAT YOU GET

- Five border styles made to sit in Eorzea: Aether ring, Barrier wall, Marching dashes, Crystal runes and FATE ember.
- Two ways to show them: always, or only when you get close to the edge of the FATE you're in.
- A warning colour that creeps in as you near the edge, an on-screen banner with the distance left and a marker on the closest point of the border.
- Borders that follow the ground over hills and slopes instead of floating through them.
- Colour, thickness, height, spacing, glow and animation for every style, with a live preview in the settings.

GETTING STARTED

Type /fatelimit (or /fl) to open the settings. /fatelimit test places a practice FATE around you so you can try every style without waiting for a real one.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you, or come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PLAYS BY THE RULES

FateLimit is purely visual: it only reads where FATEs are, which the game already shows on your map, and draws over the screen. It never moves your character or sends anything to the game. Settings are stored locally and nothing is ever uploaded.
Punchline: See the edge of every FATE, and know before you step out of it.

Author: GitHixy
Name: Chant
Description:
Chant replaces Final Fantasy XIV's cast bar with one built to be read at a glance: when you can start moving, when you can queue your next action, and what kind of spell you're casting.

WHAT YOU GET

- A slidecast window you can't miss: the bar stays red while moving would cancel your cast, and turns the moment it's safe to go.
- A get-ready phase just before that, and a warning if you start moving too early.
- The queue window marked on the bar, with the icon of the action you've already queued.
- Your spell's icon and name, coloured by what it does: damage, healing, raises, support and everything else.
- Seven built-in presets in different shapes: horizontal and vertical bars, rings and arcs, on screen or following your character. Every size, colour and piece of text can be tuned, with a live preview.
- When a cast does get cancelled, Chant tells you how early you moved, and keeps a tally of your slidecasts.
- Party raise watch: see when another healer is already raising someone.

GETTING STARTED

Type /chant to open the settings and pick a preset. /chant test plays sample casts so you can try every look without a fight.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report and opens a GitHub issue for you, or come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PLAYS BY THE RULES

Chant is purely visual: it reads the cast information the game already shows you and draws over the screen. It never casts, queues or moves anything for you, and it switches itself off in PvP. Settings and presets are stored locally and nothing is ever uploaded.
Punchline: A castbar that tells you when you can move, in the shape you like.

Author: GitHixy
Name: MoogleMap
Description:
MoogleMap lays a transparent map right over the game, the way action RPGs do: press a key and the layout around you appears on top of the world, with you in the middle, turning with your camera.

WHAT YOU GET

- The game's own maps, redrawn as a clean outline of walkable floor in dungeons, trials and alliance raids, or as the painted map with its paper background lifted away in towns and fields.
- Where there is no map to draw from, like deep dungeon floors, the layout fills in around you as you explore.
- Party members, other players, enemies (with the ones fighting you highlighted), NPCs, treasure coffers, aetherytes and gathering points, live.
- Map icons, place names, quest markers, your flag and running FATEs, with the game's own icons.
- Toggle or hold a key of your choice, zoom keys, and a smooth fade in and out.
- Size, zoom, opacity, colours, rotation and every layer can be tuned.

GETTING STARTED

Type /mooglemap (or /mmap) to open the settings and pick your key. /mmap toggle shows or hides the map, handy for a macro.
Found a bug or have an idea? Settings > Diagnostics copies a report, or come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PLAYS BY THE RULES

MoogleMap is purely visual. It only shows what the game already lets you see: hidden objects stay hidden, and it switches itself off in PvP. It never moves your character or sends anything to the game. Settings are stored locally and nothing is ever uploaded.
Punchline: A see-through map over your screen, one key away. Kupo!

Author: GitHixy
Name: Aethermeter
Description:
Aethermeter is a combat meter drawn by the game itself: no external parser to start, nothing to attach.

WHAT YOU GET

- Damage, DPS, healing, HPS, damage taken, overhealing and deaths, live while you fight.
- Every pull kept as its own segment, plus an Overall segment across them.
- A breakdown for each player: abilities, crit and direct-hit rates, biggest hits, a damage graph and a recap of every death.
- As many meter windows as you like, each on its own view.
- Streamer mode: replace every player name with their job, or with initials.
- Bars, fonts, colours and layout you can tune to taste.

GETTING STARTED

Type /meter to show or hide the meter and /meter config for settings. /meter reset clears every segment.
Found a bug or have an idea? Come and talk about it on Discord: https://discord.gg/9kjUjWDBkJ

PRIVATE BY DESIGN

Aethermeter only reads what your client already receives. It never posts to chat and never sends anything anywhere: numbers stay on your screen.
Punchline: A damage and healing meter that lives inside the game.
